Morocco
Consular help:Consular help will be provided by the Embassy of Bosnia and Herzegovina in Madrid, Espańa.
Visa required for the following traveling documentation for BH citizens (Visa shell be issued in Zagreb):
Regular passport YES
Regular biometric passport YES
Service/Official biometric passport NO up to 90 days
Diplomatic biometric passport NO up to 90 days
Embassy of the Kingdom of Morocco
Address: Pantovčak 245, 10000 Zagreb, Croatia
Tel: +385 (1) 457 82 89
Fax: +385 (1) 457 82 67
E-mail: embassy.morocco.zg@gmail.com
Citizens of the Kingdom of Morocco are required visas for regular passports when entering, exiting or travelling through Bosnia and Herzegovina. Visa shall be issued in Madrid, Spain.Citizens of the Kingdom of Morocco are not required visas for diplomatic, service and special passports when entering, exiting or travelling through Bosnia and Herzegovina up to 90 days.
Safety conditions: Morocco is seeing a growing trend in tourism and is considered a fairly safe country to travel to. However, given the current international situation and instability in neighboring regions, the possibility of terrorism or other forms of threatened security cannot be ruled out. In larger cities and tourist centers, attention should be paid to theft, pickpocketing and street fraud attempts. It is recommended to use the services of registered official guides.
Due to its geographical location, Morocco is at risk of seismic activity, and it is necessary to take into account the general recommendations for protection in the event of an earthquake.Risk zones (to be avoided): It is recommended to avoid military zones where photography is prohibited, and unmarked desert zones, including the unmarked border between Algeria and Morocco.Medium risk zones (visits with certain precautions): Isolated rural areas, where it is recommended to travel in larger groups. If you are traveling through the desert or sparsely populated rural areas, it is advisable to go in a group, preferably in several off-road vehicles.Drugs: Possession, use or trafficking of any type of narcotic drug is a serious offense that can result in years in prison.Sanitary conditions: There are a large number of private medical institutions operating in cities that can provide adequate intervention. Having travel insurance that covers Morocco is recommended.Notes: Check customs restrictions before entering the country, there are goods and items that are not allowed to enter the country.Behavior in public should not offend Islamic religious sentiments, and in this sense, it is advisable to respect local traditions, customs and laws. In certain cases, inappropriate behavior in public may result in legal sanctions.Country code: +212
